simple.meaning: יָרֵחַ (yârêach) appears 26 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a brother in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 2 Kings, Job, and 7 more, beginning at Genesis 37:9. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, kingship, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָרֵחַ (H3394) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows יָרֵחַ through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: יָרֵחַ (yârêach) / H3394 is tracked through Genesis 37:9, Deuteronomy 4:19, Deuteronomy 17:3, Joshua 10:12. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and said, “Behold, I have dreamed yet another dream: and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.”

timeline.evidenceText: He dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and said, “Behold, I have dreamed yet another dream: and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.”

and lest you lift up your eyes to the sky, and when you see the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the army of the sky, you are drawn away and worship them, and serve them, which Yahweh your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole sky.
and has gone and served other gods and worshiped them, or the sun, or the moon, or any of the stars of the sky, which I have not commanded,

Then Joshua spoke to Yahweh in the day when Yahweh delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel. He said in the sight of Israel, “Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!”

The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn’t this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.

He got rid of the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places around Jerusalem; those also who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the army of the sky.
Behold, even the moon has no brightness,
if I have seen the sun when it shined,
what is man, that you think of him?
They shall fear you while the sun endures;
In his days, the righteous shall flourish,
But you have rejected and spurned.
He appointed the moon for seasons.
The sun will not harm you by day,
the moon and stars to rule by night;
Praise him, sun and moon!
Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened,
For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going out, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
The sun will be no more your light by day;

They will spread them before the sun, the moon, and all the army of the sky, which they have loved, which they have served, after which they have walked, which they have sought, and which they have worshiped. They will not be gathered or be buried. They will be like dung on the surface of the earth.

definitions.full: H3394. yareach יָרֵחַ noun masculine Josh 10:13 moon , especially in poetry (Late Hebrew id. ; Phoenician ירח ; Assyrian iriµu , according to Pinches BOR Aug. 1888, 207 ; Ethiopic moon, month ; compare below יֶרַח ) — absolute יָרֵחַ Gen 37:9 25 t.; suffix וִיָֽרֵחֵךְ Isa 60:20 : — moon , usually named with sun Josh 10:12-13 , (poem in J E), Psa 72:5 ( יָרֵחַ וְלִפְנֵי עִםשָֿׁ֑מֶשׁ ), 89:38 (in these two, a symbol of permanence), 121:6 ; Isa 60:19 ; Hab 3:11 ; Joel 3:4 ; object of idolatrous worship Job 31:26 (+ sun); in same sense also + sun and stars Deut 4:19 ; 17:3 ; 2Kin 23:5 ; Jer 8:2 ; as determiner of feast-times Psa 104:19 (|| sun); + stars, as shining, by night 136:9 (|| sun, by day), so יָרֵחַ חֻקֹּת Jer 31:35 ; (|| id. ); elsewhere + sun and stars Gen 37:9 (E), Isa 13:10 ; Ezek 32:7 ; Joel 2:10 ; Joel 4:15; Psa 148:3 ; Eccl 12:2 ; + stars Psa 8:4 ; Job 25:5 ; with neither sun nor stars only יָרֵחַ עַדבְּֿלִי Psa 72:7 .
